problem: Prior VLN methods encode individual object/scene visual representations and miss correlations between objects within a scene and across consecutive scenes, giving incomplete spatial and temporal understanding.
motivation: Coarse-grained instructions (REVERIE, R2R-LAST) require the agent to understand the scene and its history to find the target. Modeling object relations across adjacent moments should improve instruction-vision alignment and path planning.
key_idea: Build a spatial-temporal graph linking objects' spatial positional relations at adjacent moments, and use a graph-wise attention module to select instruction-relevant graph information for planning.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so the mechanism is not verified in detail. The abstract claims that ablations show both the explicit spatial-temporal graph and graph attention improve path planning and generalization, with SR gains over the baseline of 3% on R2R-LAST and 2.92% on REVERIE.
method: Spatial-temporal graph: integrates spatial positional relationships of objects at adjacent moments to enhance understanding of historical and current scenes
Graph-wise attention module: screens visual graph information aligned with the instruction to support path planning
STE-VLN: the overall spatial-temporal-enhanced VLN model built on a baseline VLN agent (baseline not named in the abstract)

setting.backbone: STE-VLN (baseline architecture not specified in abstract)
setting.training_data: not specified in abstract (presumably REVERIE and R2R-LAST training sets)
setting.observation: not specified (likely panoramic RGB with object features)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract gives relative SR gains (+3% on R2R-LAST, +2.92% on REVERIE over the baseline) but no absolute metric values
results: STE-VLN is reported to outperform state-of-the-art methods on REVERIE and R2R-LAST across multiple metrics such as SR and RGS. It exceeds the baseline in SR by 3% on R2R-LAST and 2.92% on REVERIE. The abstract does not name the baseline or give absolute numbers.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details on the baseline, training and compute are unknown
Evaluated only on coarse-grained datasets (REVERIE, R2R-LAST)
